knowledge:
- key_parameters: filetype='bam' or 'rds' ;; binsizes=vector of bin sizes to analyze (e.g., c(100, 1000)) ;; ploidies=vector of general tumor ploidies to test (e.g., c(2, 4)) ;; penalty=factor to penalize fits at lower cellularities (default 0, recommended 0.5) ;; penploidy=factor to penalize ploidies diverging from 2 in squaremodel ;; standard=manually specified segment value corresponding to the general ploidy ;; sgc=single germline copy, specifies chromosomes present as a single germline copy (e.g., c("X", "Y") for males) to prevent fitting bias ;; exclude=vector of chromosomes to exclude from model fitting (e.g., c("X", "Y", "MT"))
- alternatives: QDNAseq is used to generate the input segmented data (ACE depends on or wraps its functions). ABSOLUTE can be used for downstream absolute copy number analysis, and getadjustedsegments can format data for it when log=TRUE.
- when_to_use: Use when you have low-coverage whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data (either aligned BAM files or pre-segmented QDNAseq RDS objects) and want to estimate tumor cellularity, determine absolute copy numbers of segments, and link copy number states to somatic mutations.
- pitfalls: Ensure the genome build used for QDNAseq bin annotations matches the build used for aligning the sequencing data. Do not rely on automated "best fit" selection; manual inspection of the likelyfits and fitpicker tables is mandatory as the lowest mathematical error is not always the biologically correct fit. Small bin sizes (<100 kbp) combined with PDF output can create extremely large files and cause crashes; use PNG instead. squaremodel can be "fithappy" and find biologically implausible ploidies; use penalty and penploidy to constrain it. Sex chromosomes must be handled carefully using the sgc argument to avoid erroneous fits in male samples.

workflows.name: run_ace_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run the full absolute copy number estimation pipeline on a directory of BAM or RDS files to generate diagnostic plots and fitpicker tables.
input: Aligned BAM files in a directory OR segmented QDNAseq RDS files.
workflows.stages: 1. Run runACE to process files, perform segmentation (if BAM), and calculate fits across specified ploidies and bin sizes. 2. Inspect output directories, likelyfits, and fitpicker tables to select the most likely models.
workflows.code:
# specify the directory containing your bam-files
userpath <- tempdir()
# if you do not want the output in the same directory, use argument outputdir
runACE(userpath, filetype='bam', binsizes = c(100, 1000),
       ploidies = c(2,4), imagetype='png')

data("copyNumbersSegmented")
# specify the directory in which to create the output
userpath <- tempdir()
saveRDS(file.path(userpath,"copyNumbersSegmented.rds"))
runACE(userpath, filetype='rds', ploidies = c(2,4), imagetype='png')

workflows.name: single_sample_refinement
workflows.intent: Perform detailed model fitting, standard adjustment, and visualization for a single sample to find the optimal cellularity and ploidy.
workflows.stages: 1. Fit a single model using singlemodel. 2. Plot the copy number profile using singleplot. 3. Convert object to template using objectsampletotemplate. 4. Perform 2D grid search over ploidy and cellularity using squaremodel.
workflows.code:
data("copyNumbersSegmented")
object <- copyNumbersSegmented
model1 <- singlemodel(object, QDNAseqobjectsample = 1)
bestfit1 <- model1$minima[tail(which(model1$rerror==min(model1$rerror)), 1)]
besterror1 <- min(model1$rerror)
lastfit1 <- tail(model1$minima, 1)
lasterror1 <- tail(model1$rerror, 1)
singleplot(object, QDNAseqobjectsample = 1, cellularity = bestfit1, 
           error = besterror1, standard = model1$standard, 
           title = "sample1 - binsize 1000 kbp - 379776 reads - 2N fit 1")
singleplot(object, QDNAseqobjectsample = 1, cellularity = lastfit1, 
           error = lasterror1, standard = model1$standard, 
           title = "sample1 - binsize 1000 kbp - 379776 reads - 2N fit 7")
model1$errorplot + ggtitle("sample1 - errorlist") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
model2 <- singlemodel(object, QDNAseqobjectsample = 2)
singleplot(object, QDNAseqobjectsample = 2, 0.38, 0.183, 
           title = "sample2 - binsize 1000 kbp - 369331 reads - 2N fit 3")
singleplot(object, QDNAseqobjectsample = 2, 0.94, 0.998, 
           title = "sample2 - binsize 1000 kbp - 369331 reads - 2N fit 6")
model2$errorplot +	ggtitle("sample2 - errorlist") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

model <- singlemodel(object, QDNAseqobjectsample = 2, ploidy = 3)
ls(model)
model$minima
model$rerror
model$errorplot
singleplot(object, QDNAseqobjectsample = 2, cellularity = 0.46, ploidy = 3)

template <- objectsampletotemplate(object, index = 2)
head(template)
head(na.exclude(template))
median(na.exclude(template$segments))
unique(na.exclude(template$segments))
segmentdata <- rle(as.vector(na.exclude(template$segments)))
plot(rep(segmentdata$values, segmentdata$lengths))
model <- singlemodel(template, ploidy = 2, standard = 0.8105095)
data.frame(model$minima, model$rerror)
singleplot(template, cellularity = 0.46, ploidy = 2, standard = 0.8105095)

sqmodel <- squaremodel(template)
ls(sqmodel)
sqmodel$matrixplot + ggtitle("Sky on fire")
head(sqmodel$minimadf, 10)
squaremodel(template, penalty = 0.5, penploidy = 0.5)$matrixplot
sqmodel <- squaremodel(template, prows = 150, ptop = 3.3, pbottom = 1.8, 
                       penalty = 0.5, penploidy = 0.5)
sqmodel$matrixplot
head(sqmodel$minimadf, 10)
singleplot(template, cellularity = 0.41, ploidy = 2.08)

workflows.name: variant_and_segment_annotation
workflows.intent: Extract adjusted copy number segments and link them to somatic mutations or specific genomic locations.
input: Segmented template data frame, variant/mutation data frame.
workflows.stages: 1. Extract adjusted segments using getadjustedsegments. 2. Link mutations to copy number segments and calculate mutant copies using linkvariants. 3. Query specific genomic locations using analyzegenomiclocations.
workflows.code:
segmentdf <- getadjustedsegments(template, cellularity = 0.38)
head(segmentdf)

Gene <- c("CASP8", "CDKN2A", "TP53")
Chromosome <- c(2, 9, 17)
Position <- c(202149589, 21971186, 7574003)
Frequency <- c(47.46, 36.28, 43.48)
variantdf <- data.frame(Gene, Chromosome, Position, Frequency)
linkvariants(variantdf, segmentdf, cellularity = 0.38, 
                 chrindex = 2, posindex = 3, freqindex = 4)

analyzegenomiclocations(segmentdf, Chromosome = 1, Position = 26365569)

chr <- c(1,2,3)
pos <- c(2000000,4000000,6000000)
analyzegenomiclocations(segmentdf, Chromosome = chr, Position = pos)

freq <- c(38,19,0)
analyzegenomiclocations(segmentdf=segmentdf, cellularity = 0.38, 
                        Chromosome = chr, Position = pos, Frequency = freq)

workflows.name: batch_post_analysis
workflows.intent: Automate segment adjustment and variant linking across a large dataset using a pre-defined models file.
input: Segmented QDNAseq object, models.tsv (tab-delimited file with sample, cellularity, ploidy, standard), sample-specific mutation files.
workflows.stages: 1. Create a models file and mutation files. 2. Run postanalysisloop to batch-process all samples.
workflows.code:
# Set the correct path
userpath <- tempdir()
# This function needs a models-file, which should like like this
sample <- c("sample1", "sample2")
cellularity <- c(0.79, 0.38)
ploidy <- c(2, 2)
standard <- c(1, 1)
models <- data.frame(sample, cellularity, ploidy, standard)
write.table(models, file.path(userpath, "models.tsv"), quote = FALSE,
            sep = "\t", na = "", row.names = FALSE)
# Let's make sure we have some mutation data to analyze
# For simplicity, I will just use the same mutation data for both samples
write.table(mutationdf, file.path(userpath, "sample1_mutations.tsv"),
            quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", na = "", row.names = FALSE)
write.table(mutationdf, file.path(userpath, "sample2_mutations.tsv"),
            quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", na = "", row.names = FALSE)
# Let's go!
postanalysisloop(object, inputdir = userpath, postfix = "_mutations",
                 chrindex = 2, posindex = 3, freqindex = 4,
                 outputdir = file.path(userpath,"output_loop"), imagetype = 'png')
